notes: This is the real one in the batch and it is not a pandemic story at all. The letter says Mitec Powertrain, Inc. and Mitec Automotive, Inc. 'are permanently closing their facility located in Findlay, OH 45840', and gives the reason: 'The closure is a result of business being transferred from Mitec's largest customer to another supplier, who is moving the production lines to Mexico and Canada. A petition for TAA certification has been filed with the U.S. Department of Labor.' COVID is not mentioned. The letter is signed by Scott Eisenberg of Amherst Partners as Chief Restructuring Officer, which is itself a distress signal. caveat: The funded Findlay plant closed permanently, and JobsOhio got all of the money back: $200,000 paid in FY2019 and $200,000 reversed in FY2020. The row counts as a company and carries $0. The closure was not the pandemic: the letter gives the cause as the largest customer moving production to Mexico and Canada, and it is signed by a chief restructuring officer.
